slides.heading: How Brain-Computer Interfaces Are Advancing
slides.body: The technology that lets your brain talk directly to machines — and what it means for humanity

slides.heading: What Is a Brain-Computer Interface?
slides.body: A brain-computer interface (BCI) is a direct communication pathway between the brain and an external device. It reads electrical signals from neurons and translates them into commands — no muscles or movement required.

slides.heading: Two Types: Invasive vs. Non-Invasive
slides.body: Invasive BCIs use implanted electrodes for high-resolution signals — like Neuralink's chip. Non-invasive BCIs use EEG headsets worn on the scalp, offering lower precision but no surgery. Each trade-off serves different use cases.

slides.heading: The Neuralink Milestone
slides.body: In 2024, Neuralink implanted its first chip in a human patient, who could control a computer cursor using only thoughts. By 2026, multiple patients have regained digital independence, demonstrating real-world viability of implantable BCIs.

slides.heading: Restoring Lost Function
slides.body: BCIs are transforming medicine by restoring movement to paralyzed patients and speech to those with ALS. Neural bypass systems re-route signals around damaged spinal cords, letting patients move robotic limbs or type with their minds.

slides.heading: Memory and Cognitive Enhancement
slides.body: Researchers are developing BCIs that can boost memory by stimulating the hippocampus at the right moment. DARPA-funded studies showed a 37% improvement in memory recall in participants using closed-loop neural stimulation systems.

slides.heading: AI Is the Secret Ingredient
slides.body: Modern BCIs rely on machine learning to decode messy neural signals into clean commands. AI models trained on individual brain patterns can interpret intentions with increasing accuracy — and adapt in real time as the brain changes.

slides.heading: The Ethical Minefield
slides.body: BCIs raise urgent questions: Who owns your neural data? Can employers or governments access your thoughts? Mental privacy — 'cognitive liberty' — is now a serious legal and ethical frontier as BCIs move toward consumer adoption.

slides.heading: Consumer BCIs Are Coming
slides.body: Companies like Emotiv, Muse, and Neurosity already sell EEG headsets for focus and meditation. As precision improves, BCIs may replace keyboards and touchscreens — enabling thought-to-text input and hands-free device control within this decade.

slides.heading: The Mind-Machine Frontier
slides.body: Brain-computer interfaces are moving from science fiction to clinic to living room. Understanding the technology today means being prepared — as both a user and a citizen — for the choices ahead.
